question.text: A farmer's urban agricultural land was compulsorily acquired by the State Government for a highway project. He received Rs.45,00,000 as compensation. What is the tax treatment of the capital gains arising from this compulsory acquisition?

answer.text: Fully exempt under Section 10(37) as it is compulsory acquisition of urban agricultural land
Taxable as long-term capital gains at 20% with indexation
Exempt only if the compensation is reinvested in another agricultural land within 2 years
Exempt only up to Rs.20,00,000 and balance taxable

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 10(37) exempts capital gains arising from compulsory acquisition of urban agricultural land in India, subject to conditions including agricultural use during the two years immediately preceding the transfer and receipt of compensation on or after 1 April 2004. There is no monetary ceiling and no reinvestment requirement under this provision. Note that rural agricultural land in India is not a capital asset at all under the Act, so no capital gain arises in the first place; Section 10(37) is the relevant exemption when the land is urban. The Trap: Option B ignores the specific exemption provision. Option C imports the reinvestment condition that belongs to Section 54B (voluntary sale of agricultural land), not Section 10(37). Option D invents a monetary cap that is not part of the section. Note: Distinguish 10(37) (compulsory acquisition of urban agricultural land, full exemption) from 54B (voluntary sale of agricultural land, exemption conditional on reinvestment) and from the basic rule that rural agricultural land is outside the capital-asset definition altogether.
